_comment: Curriculum order. The map order teaches the economy: each map's payout tier is what affords the marker that the NEXT map's skill requires.
_order: The curriculum, ordered by engagement distance: Speedball 16, Dustline 18.48, Urban 27, Woods 38.72, Holdfast 45.76 metres -- each map is the next step out, and MapsSpec asserts the ordering holds against the declared bands. Dustline, Woods and Holdfast were rescaled to 88% on 2026-09-07 and their bands moved with them; Speedball and Urban were left at full size because shrinking them inverted the way they punish trading. See each map's _scale note.

palette._note: Saturated, strong silhouettes, 0-255 RGB. Surfaces are no longer uniformly flat plastic -- WorldBuilder maps each key to a material (grass, sand, concrete, timber, slate) and inflatables get a vinyl sheen -- but the rule that cover reads darker than ground, and bots read as the most saturated thing on screen, still governs every value here.
palette._undeclared: brush, stone and containerRust were in use on Woods, Holdfast and Dustline but had never been declared here, so every thicket, copse, outcrop and rusted screen was falling back to concrete grey on smooth plastic. Woods and Holdfast were rendering their treelines as pale grey boxes.

assembly._note: Nav edges are not hand-listed. The builder links any two nav nodes within navLinkRadiusMetres whose connecting segment is not blocked by a cover volume. Hand-authoring 80 edges per map is how maps stop getting edited.

lighting._comment: Look tuning. The palette stays saturated and the silhouettes stay strong; what changed is that the light is doing work. Future technology gives real-time shadows and light bounce, atmosphere gives distance haze so a 70 m sightline in Woods reads as far away, and a little bloom sells the gloss on the vinyl.

speedball._note: Tournament field on a bright afternoon. Short sightlines, so almost no haze -- nothing should be softened at 20 m.

urban._note: Dusty and hot. Warmer ambient, more haze bouncing off the sand, longer focus.

woods._note: Late overcast light under a treeline. The heavy haze is doing a job here: it is what makes a 70 m shot LOOK like 70 m, which is the whole lesson of this map.

dustline._note: Desert freight yard, mid-afternoon, hard light. Very little haze up close so the container corners stay crisp, but a hot sand glare on everything.

holdfast._note: Deep woods valley, low sun behind the north keep. The heaviest haze in the game and it is load-bearing: a 110 m lane has to LOOK like 110 m or nobody can judge the holdover it needs.
